_healthy_template.symptoms: Foliage shows uniform green coloration, turgid leaf structure, and no visible lesions, chlorosis, mold, or pest feeding damage.
organic_treatment: No curative treatment required; continue balanced compost or vermicompost top-dressing.
Maintain beneficial microbial activity with periodic seaweed or compost tea foliar feeds if appropriate.
chemical_treatment: No fungicide or insecticide application needed.
prevention: Maintain adequate plant spacing for airflow and avoid overhead evening irrigation.
Inspect lower leaves weekly for early signs of spots, webbing, or insect eggs.
Rotate crops seasonally and sanitize pruning tools between beds.

_default_disease_template.symptoms: Abnormal leaf spotting, discoloration, necrotic lesions, wilting, or visible pest injury observed on plant tissue.
organic_treatment: Prune and destroy heavily affected leaves away from the field (do not compost diseased debris).
Apply cold-pressed neem oil (0.5-1%) or potassium bicarbonate / copper soap per label guidance in cool evening hours.
chemical_treatment: Consult a local agricultural extension officer to confirm the exact pathogen or pest before spraying.
Use a targeted, registered fungicide or insecticide following label dosage and pre-harvest intervals.
prevention: Water at the root zone in the morning so foliage dries rapidly.
Practice a 2-3 year crop rotation and plant certified disease-free seeds or resistant varieties.
Control weeds and volunteer host plants around field borders.

_default_pest_template.symptoms: Chewing holes, stippling, curled leaves, honeydew residue, or visible insect larvae/adults on stems, leaves, or fruits.
organic_treatment: Hand-pick visible caterpillars/beetles or dislodge soft-bodied insects with a strong water spray.
Apply neem oil (azadirachtin), insecticidal soap, or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) for caterpillar pests.
chemical_treatment: Use selective, low-impact insecticides (e.g., spinosad or targeted label-approved actives) only when pest thresholds are exceeded.
Avoid spraying during active bee pollination hours.
prevention: Install yellow/blue sticky traps or pheromone traps for early pest monitoring.
Encourage natural predators (ladybugs, lacewings, parasitic wasps) via flowering border strips.
Remove crop residues promptly after harvest to break pest pupation cycles.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark velvety spots on leaves and fruit that turn brown, corky, and cracked; heavily infected leaves curl and drop early.
organic_treatment: Apply wettable sulfur or liquid lime-sulfur sprays starting at green-tip stage through early petal fall.
Spray aerated compost tea or potassium bicarbonate on young foliage during wet spring periods.
chemical_treatment: Apply protectant fungicides such as captan or mancozeb at 7-10 day intervals during rainy spring weather.
Rotate with systemic fungicides (e.g., myclobutanil or difenoconazole) to avoid resistance.
prevention: Rake and shred or burn fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering fungal spores.
Prune tree canopy annually to improve sunlight penetration and air circulation.
Plant scab-resistant cultivars such as Liberty, Enterprise, or GoldRush.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple flecks on leaves enlarging into 'frog-eye' brown lesions; firm brown-to-black concentric rings on rotting fruit and sunken bark cankers.
organic_treatment: Prune out dead wood, twig dieback, and mummified fruit at least 15 cm below visible cankers.
Apply organic copper sprays early in the season where permitted.
chemical_treatment: Apply captan, thiophanate-methyl, or strobilurin fungicides from tight-cluster through cover sprays.
Follow orchard spray schedules strictly during warm, humid summer months.
prevention: Remove mummified fruits from trees and orchard floor before spring bud break.
Prevent bark injuries from equipment or sunscald and disinfect pruning shears with 70% alcohol.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surfaces that develop tiny black dots and tube-like projections on leaf undersides.
organic_treatment: Apply wettable sulfur or copper-based fungicides preventatively when nearby juniper/cedar galls swell after spring rain.
chemical_treatment: Apply myclobutanil or mancozeb from pink-bud stage through 2-3 weeks post-petal fall.
prevention: Remove nearby Eastern red cedar or juniper trees within 300 meters if feasible, or prune galls off ornamentals in late winter.
Choose rust-resistant apple varieties.

Cherry___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery fungal patches on young leaves and shoots causing upward leaf curling, stunting, and premature drop.
organic_treatment: Spray horticultural oil, neem oil, or potassium bicarbonate thoroughly covering leaf undersides.
Apply micronized sulfur (avoid when temperatures exceed 30 C to prevent leaf scorch).
chemical_treatment: Rotate DMI (myclobutanil) and QoI fungicides at 10-14 day intervals during shoot flush.
prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization that triggers dense succulent shoots.
Prune interior water sprouts to reduce humidity inside the canopy.

Corn___Gray_leaf_spot.symptoms: Rectangular, narrow tan-to-gray lesions bounded sharply by leaf veins; severe infections coalesce and blight entire leaves.
organic_treatment: Remove severely infected lower leaves in small garden plots and apply biological Trichoderma or Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicides early.
chemical_treatment: Apply azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin, or propiconazole at VT-R1 (tassel to silking) if disease reaches the third leaf below the ear.
prevention: Rotate corn with soybeans or non-host crops for at least 1-2 years.
Incorporate infected corn residue via tillage or select hybrids with high GLS resistance ratings.

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Small, elongated cinnamon-brown pustules scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces that rupture to release powdery spores.
organic_treatment: Dust or spray sulfur early in sweet corn plots when pustules first appear on lower leaves.
chemical_treatment: Apply triazole or strobilurin fungicides (e.g., azoxystrobin + propiconazole) if high pustule density occurs prior to silking.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids and avoid late planting dates that coincide with peak spore arrival.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan necrotic lesions (2.5-15 cm) running parallel to leaf margins.
organic_treatment: Apply Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or copper-based organic sprays protectively in high-value sweet corn.
chemical_treatment: Spray strobilurin + triazole fungicide mixtures between tasseling and early silking when lesions appear on lower canopy.
prevention: Use hybrids carrying Ht resistance genes, rotate away from continuous corn, and manage overwintering residue.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular leaf spots with dark borders and tiny black pycnidia; berries turn brown, shrivel into hard black mummies.
organic_treatment: Apply copper hydroxide or sulfur sprays protectively prior to rain events from bud break until veraison.
chemical_treatment: Use mancozeb, captan, or myclobutanil on a 7-14 day schedule during warm, wet bloom and early fruit set.
prevention: Remove all mummified berries and infected canes during winter pruning.
Train vines and pull leaves around fruit clusters to maximize sunlight and rapid drying.

Grape___Esca_Black_Measles.symptoms: Interveinal 'tiger-stripe' yellowing or reddening on leaves, small dark spots on berries, and vascular wood streaking inside trunks.
organic_treatment: Apply Trichoderma-based wound protectants immediately to fresh pruning cuts.
Remove and destroy dead cordons or severely symptomatic vines.
chemical_treatment: No curative chemical spray reverses internal wood infection; protect pruning wounds with approved sealing pastes.
prevention: Prune late in dormancy during dry weather and avoid large pruning cuts whenever possible.
Sanitize shears between vines.

Grape___Leaf_blight.symptoms: Irregular dull-red to dark-brown blotches that merge into large dead patches along leaf edges, causing premature defoliation.
organic_treatment: Apply Bordeaux mixture or fixed copper sprays after heavy rain events in late summer.
chemical_treatment: Apply mancozeb or captan if defoliation threatens sugar accumulation prior to harvest (respect PHI).
prevention: Improve trellis airflow, manage canopy vigor, and destroy fallen diseased leaves.

Orange___Citrus_greening.symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy yellow mottling across leaves, twig dieback, and small, lopsided fruit that stays green at the bottom and tastes bitter.
organic_treatment: Control Asian citrus psyllid vectors using neem oil, horticultural oils, and kaolin clay barriers.
Note: No organic cure exists once a tree is systemically infected.
chemical_treatment: Manage psyllid populations strictly via coordinated area-wide insecticide programs (e.g., imidacloprid, cyantraniliprole).
Report suspected cases to local agricultural quarantine authorities.
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock grown under screenhouses.
Promptly remove and destroy confirmed infected trees to protect neighboring orchards.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked angular leaf spots turning dark purple/black and dropping out ('shot-hole' appearance); sunken cracks on fruit.
organic_treatment: Apply low-rate fixed copper sprays at dormancy and early leaf drop; avoid high-rate copper during active foliage to prevent phytotoxicity.
chemical_treatment: Apply oxytetracycline (where registered) from shuck split through cover sprays during wet windy periods.
prevention: Plant bacterial-spot-resistant peach cultivars and establish windbreaks to reduce sand-blasting leaf wounds.
Avoid sandy, exposed sites with high wind erosion.

Pepper_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked circular lesions on leaves that turn dark brown/black with yellow halos; raised scabby cork-like spots on fruit.
organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves carefully when foliage is dry.
Apply copper soap + Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicide tank mixes weekly in humid weather.
chemical_treatment: Spray copper hydroxide tank-mixed with mancozeb (where legally permitted) on a 5-7 day preventive interval.
prevention: Use hot-water-treated or certified pathogen-free seed and resistant bell pepper varieties.
Avoid working in wet fields and rotate out of Solanaceae for 2-3 years.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown circular leaf spots showing distinct concentric 'target-board' rings, typically starting on older lower leaves with surrounding yellowing.
organic_treatment: Remove lower infected leaves and apply copper fungicide or Bacillus subtilis sprays every 7-10 days.
chemical_treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin/difenoconazole starting at row closure or first lesion sighting.
prevention: Maintain adequate nitrogen and potassium nutrition (stressed plants succumb rapidly).
Rotate potatoes for 3 years and use drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Rapidly expanding dark water-soaked blotches on leaves and stems with pale green borders and white downy mold on undersides during humid mornings.
organic_treatment: Immediately pull and bag severely infected plants so spores do not spread across the field.
Apply protective copper hydroxide sprays ahead of cool, wet weather.
chemical_treatment: Apply systemic/translaminar oomycete fungicides (e.g., fluopicolide, cymoxanil, dimethomorph, or mandipropamid) alternated with mancozeb on a strict 5-7 day schedule.
prevention: Plant certified blight-free seed tubers and destroy volunteer potatoes and cull piles.
Hill soil well over tubers to prevent spore wash-down and harvest after vines are fully dead.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Talcum-like white powdery spots on upper and lower leaf surfaces and petioles, causing premature yellowing and reduced fruit sweetness.
organic_treatment: Spray neem oil, horticultural oil, potassium bicarbonate, or diluted wettable sulfur (below 29 C).
chemical_treatment: Rotate myclobutanil, triflumizole, or cyflufenamid with protectant chlorothalonil or sulfur.
prevention: Select powdery-mildew-resistant squash cultivars and plant in full sun with wide spacing.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Numerous irregular dark purple blotches on leaves that coalesce, turning entire leaves reddish-brown and dried ('scorched').
organic_treatment: Mow and remove infected older leaves after harvest; apply copper or sulfur sprays during spring growth.
chemical_treatment: Apply captan, dodine, or strobilurin fungicides from early bloom through fruiting.
prevention: Establish beds with certified disease-free crowns, use drip irrigation, and renovate beds post-harvest.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Greasy dark spots (2-3 mm) on leaves often with yellow halos causing leaf drop; raised black scabs on green fruits.
organic_treatment: Prune lower leaves for airflow and spray copper octanoate + Bacillus bio-fungicide early in the morning.
chemical_treatment: Apply fixed copper + mancozeb tank mix preventively every 5-7 days during rainy periods.
prevention: Sanitize stakes/cages, soak seeds in 50 C water for 25 minutes before sowing, and avoid handling wet plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown lesions with concentric rings ('bullseye' pattern) starting on oldest lower leaves, leading to yellowing and defoliation.
organic_treatment: Prune infected bottom leaves up to the first fruit cluster and mulch soil to block splash-borne spores.
Apply copper soap or Serenade (Bacillus subtilis) every 7 days.
chemical_treatment: Rotate chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin at 7-10 day intervals.
prevention: Stake or trellis tomatoes off the ground, mulch with straw, and practice 3-year non-solanaceous crop rotation.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large irregular dark water-soaked patches on leaves and dark greasy lesions on stems, accompanied by white fuzzy growth underneath in wet weather.
organic_treatment: Remove and bag infected plants immediately; apply copper hydroxide prophylactically on healthy adjacent plants.
chemical_treatment: Apply oomycete-targeted fungicides (mandipropamid, cymoxanil, or propamocarb) immediately upon local blight alerts.
prevention: Grow in high tunnels or rain shelters if available, plant resistant varieties (e.g., Mountain Magic, Defiant), and never compost infected vines.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow-green blotches on upper leaf surfaces matched by olive-green to velvety purple-gray mold on the underside.
organic_treatment: Increase greenhouse ventilation aggressively and remove lower affected leaves.
Apply copper or potassium bicarbonate sprays covering leaf undersides.
chemical_treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or difenoconazole where permitted in protected or field tomatoes.
prevention: Keep relative humidity below 85% via ventilation fans and morning drip irrigation; select Cf-resistant hybrids.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (2-5 mm) with dark brown edges and tan/gray centers containing tiny black fruiting bodies.
organic_treatment: Strip infected lower leaves and disinfect shears; spray copper fungicide or sulfur at 7-day intervals.
chemical_treatment: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb starting when lower foliage first shows spotting.
prevention: Control nightshade weeds, mulch soil heavily, and sanitize trellises every season.

Tomato___Spider_mites.symptoms: Fine yellow/white stippling on upper leaf surfaces, bronzing, and delicate silken webbing beneath leaves during hot, dry weather.
organic_treatment: Blast leaf undersides with cool water to break webs and dislodge mites.
Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, or release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).
chemical_treatment: Use selective miticides (abamectin, bifenazate, or spiromesifen) targeting leaf undersides; avoid broad-spectrum pyrethroids that flare mites.
prevention: Reduce plant drought stress and dust on field roads, and avoid killing beneficial predatory insects.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small pinpoint necrotic spots enlarging to brown target-like lesions on leaves and sunken dark spots on fruit.
organic_treatment: Remove lower diseased leaves and apply copper or Bacillus bio-fungicide sprays.
chemical_treatment: Apply azoxystrobin, boscalid, or chlorothalonil when canopy closes.
prevention: Ensure wide plant spacing and clean up all tomato crop debris post-harvest.

Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe upward curling and cupping of young leaves, bright yellow margins, stunted bushy growth, and flower drop; spread by whiteflies.
organic_treatment: Uproot and bag symptomatic young plants immediately to stop whiteflies from spreading the virus.
Control silverleaf whiteflies with neem oil, insecticidal soap, and yellow sticky traps.
chemical_treatment: Control whitefly vectors using systemic neonicotinoids or flupyradifurone/pyriproxyfen rotated by mode of action.
prevention: Use Ty-gene resistant tomato hybrids, reflective silver mulches, and insect-proof seedling nurseries.

Tomato___Mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light- and dark-green mosaic mottling on leaves, distorted 'fern-leaf' narrowing, and uneven fruit ripening.
organic_treatment: Rogue out infected plants carefully and wash hands/tools thoroughly with 10% skim milk or trisodium phosphate solution.
chemical_treatment: No chemical spray cures plant viruses; focus strictly on sanitation and vector exclusion.
prevention: Do not handle tobacco products before touching tomato plants, use TMV-resistant varieties, and disinfect tools frequently.

Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked stripes along leaf margins that turn yellow-white and dry out; milky bacterial ooze may appear on young lesions in morning dew.
organic_treatment: Drain standing paddy water temporarily and apply Pseudomonas fluorescens biocontrol spray or copper-based organic formulations.
chemical_treatment: Avoid unnecessary sprays once widespread; consult extension services for bactericide/copper oxychloride options at early onset.
prevention: Plant resistant rice cultivars, avoid excessive nitrogen top-dressing, and keep bunds free of weed hosts.

Rice___Brown_spot.symptoms: Oval sesame-seed-shaped dark brown spots with gray centers and yellow halos on leaves and glumes.
organic_treatment: Improve soil potassium/silicon nutrition and apply Trichoderma or neem-based foliar extracts.
chemical_treatment: Treat seeds before sowing; apply propiconazole or iprodione + carbendazim at booting if severe.
prevention: Correct nutrient-deficient or drought-stressed soils and sow clean, treated seed.

Rice___Leaf_blast.symptoms: Diamond/spindle-shaped lesions with gray-white centers and dark brown borders; severe infections kill seedlings or cause neck rot.
organic_treatment: Maintain steady shallow flood water (avoid intermittent drought stress) and apply silicon soil amendments.
chemical_treatment: Apply tricyclazole, isoprothiolane, or azoxystrobin at early lesion emergence or booting stage.
prevention: Split nitrogen applications, avoid overly dense seeding, and grow blast-resistant varieties.

Rice___Leaf_smut.symptoms: Small, slightly raised angular black spots scattered on both sides of rice leaves, typically appearing late in the season.
organic_treatment: Generally minor economic impact; remove heavily infected crop straw post-harvest.
chemical_treatment: Seldom requires targeted spray; broad-spectrum triazoles used for sheath/brown spot also suppress leaf smut.
prevention: Balance nitrogen fertilization and practice clean field sanitation after harvest.

Cassava___Bacterial_blight.symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots, blighting, wilting, gum exudates on stems, and shoot tip dieback.
organic_treatment: Prune and burn infected stems; disinfect machetes between plants with bleach or flame.
chemical_treatment: No systemic chemical cure; apply copper bactericides only in nurseries to limit spread.
prevention: Use disease-free stem cuttings from healthy mother blocks and intercrop cassava with maize or legumes.

Cassava___Mosaic_disease.symptoms: Severe yellow-green mosaic mottling, twisted deformed leaflets, and stunted plants yielding small roots.
organic_treatment: Rogue infected young plants early and manage whitefly vectors with neem or insecticidal soap.
chemical_treatment: No cure for infected plants; target whiteflies in seed multiplication plots if advised locally.
prevention: Plant CMD-resistant cassava varieties and strictly select symptom-free planting stakes.

Pest___Aphids.symptoms: Clusters of tiny soft-bodied green, black, or yellow insects on tender shoots and leaf undersides; curled leaves and sticky honeydew.
organic_treatment: Blast colonies with water, spray insecticidal soap or neem oil, and preserve ladybugs and hoverfly larvae.
chemical_treatment: Apply selective aphicides (e.g., flonicamid or pymetrozine) only if natural predators fail to keep numbers below threshold.
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen flushing, use reflective mulches on seedlings, and plant insectary flowers (alyssum, dill).

Pest___Armyworm.symptoms: Ragged defoliation, skeletonized young leaves ('windowpaning'), dark frass pellets in whorls, and striped caterpillars feeding at dusk.
organic_treatment: Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt kurstaki) or spinosad directly into plant whorls when larvae are small.
chemical_treatment: Apply emamectin benzoate, chlorantraniliprole, or spinetoram early in larval instar stages.
prevention: Monitor pheromone traps weekly, encourage parasitic wasps and birds, and scout leaf undersides for egg masses.
